articles.title: Stellantis taking Unifor to court over alleged obstruction of environmental assessment
articles.summary: The ongoing dispute over the sale of Stellantis's Brampton, Ont., assembly plant is heading to court, as the automaker has filed a lawsuit alleging Unifor is impeding an environmental assessment necessary to the transaction.

articles.title: Anthem singer apologizes for botched O Canada lyrics at Leafs game against Islanders
articles.summary: The anthem singer at the Toronto Maple Leafs game against New York Monday night apologized on social media after singing the wrong lyrics to the Canadian national anthem.

articles.title: Spike in emissions a major setback in GTA climate goals: report
articles.summary: A more polluting energy grid and rising demand for gas heating during a colder winter drove the largest annual spike in planet-warming emissions in at least a decade across the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area, a new report found, putting the region further off track of its climate goals.

articles.title: Police wouldn't have arrested Francique if he stayed home, detective tells inquest
articles.summary: A coroner's inquest into the death of a Black man who was shot by police in Mississauga, Ont., heard Monday that officers did not necessarily plan to arrest him that night nearly seven years ago.

articles.title: City of Mississauga to implement hiring restrictions effective immediately
articles.summary: One week into the term of Mississauga's new mayor and hiring restrictions are going into effect at the city. It comes after staff were directed by Mayor Alvin Tedjo to freeze property taxes for the 2027 and 2028 budgets.

articles.title: Toronto's top bureaucrat leaving city hall, Chow uses 'strong mayor' powers to appoint interim replacement
articles.summary: Toronto Mayor Olivia Chow has signed off on an overhaul of some of Toronto’s top bureaucratic roles, including city manager, as part of a restructuring of the city's internal operations.
